messages:
priya: heads-up: we're planning a small schema addition to the audit events to support line-level provenance for embeddings + encryption metadata. will kick off a backfill and customer validation phase tomorrow. pinging sec + infra for questions.

sam: outline? what fields are we adding exactly?

priya: main additions: `event_fingerprint` (stable id for dedupe), `encryption.kms_key_id` (nullable), and `logline_source` (values: api, dedicated, private). also a `schema_version: 3` bump. intended to be additive only.

elliot: is `encryption.kms_key_id` the raw ARN? or a hashed id? customer concerns about exposing key identifiers.

priya: good call. we'll store only the KMS key alias or customer-provided id, not the full ARN. docs will say "alias or short id only" and we will redact on export unless customer explicitly requests key material.

carla: from support: customers ask for proof of who requested a key operation. will `event_fingerprint` be stable across retries?

priya: yes - deterministic from request id + actor id + timestamp bucket. retries get same fingerprint so dedupe in SIEMs is easier. we'll include `retry_count` too.

sec-oncall: vulnerability triage note: make sure the backfill job doesn't leak plaintext data into logs. any transformation must run in VPC with KMS envelope keys.

sam: infra note: backfill plan is incremental: 1) apply schema migration (add optional fields), 2) run backfill in read-only window per region with throttling, 3) validate sample set, 4) customer opt-in for export. Will open a runbook.

audit-bot: scheduled job created: `audit-backfill-v3` starting 2026-03-22T02:00Z. job id: abf-20260322-1 ✅

priya: customer-facing validation: we want a simple API `/audit/validate-event` that accepts a sample event and returns schema conformance + redaction suggestions. Carla, can you draft the wording? aim for plain english and examples.

carla: yep. will draft with examples showing `encryption.kms_key_id` redaction and `event_fingerprint` use cases. also include migration FAQ: "Will my SIEM break?" answer: additive fields ignored by most parsers, but we provide mapping docs.

elliot: RBAC change: adding a new role `audit_viewer` who can read enriched audit events but not export key ids. Admins can grant it. Need to update docs and IAM mapping. Also we should log role assignment events into the audit stream (obviously).

sec-oncall: incident response addition: if backfill job sees >0.1% malformed events, it auto-pauses and pages sec-oncall and infra. default slack alert channel: #incidents.

priya: sample payload (for docs):
```json
{
  "schema_version": "3",
  "timestamp": "2026-03-22T02:12:34Z",
  "actor": "team-service-account",
  "action": "generate.embedding",
  "event_fingerprint": "sha256:0a1b2c3d...",
  "encryption": {"kms_key_id": "alias/cust-1234"},
  "logline_source": "dedicated",
  "retry_count": 0
}
```

sam: docs checklist for release notes: short summary, migration steps, backfill schedule, RBAC changes, how to opt-out of KMS id collection, link to `/audit/validate-event`, compatibility note for SIEMs.

carla: I'll prepare the customer email + support playbook. proposed phrasing: "We're rolling out richer audit events to help with forensics and compliance. No action needed for most customers; see validation API and mapping guide."

priya: final ops ask: please add an automated smoke test that posts a sample event to `/audit/validate-event` and asserts 200 + `schema_version: 3` in the response. infra-bot please create the pipeline job.

infra-bot: created pipeline `ci/audit-validate-smoke` -> link: https://ci.redwood.example/runs/abf-smoke-177900.

sam: I'll own the rollout and publish a short changelog entry once the backfill completes. tagging @carla for customer comms and @sec-oncall for signoff before we unpause. :thumbsup:

priya: thanks all. leaving thread open for any follow-ups.
